questions.stem: Which of the following is a false statement regarding antidiuretic Hormone function?

options.label: A
options.text: Terlipressin is better than desmopressin for esophageal variceal bleeding

options.label: B
options.text: Desmopressin is not much effective against nephrogenic diabetes insipidus

options.label: C
options.text: Amiloride used for lithium-induced diabetes insipidus

options.label: D
options.text: Desmopressin is used for both pituitary and renal diabetes insipidus

questions.answerText: Desmopressin is used for both pituitary and renal diabetes insipidus
questions.solutionHtml:
Desmopressin is used for both pituitary and renal diabetes insipidus

Desmopressin works by replacing vasopressin a hormone that is normally produced in the body to help balance the amount of water and salt.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 643

questions.stem: Desmopressin is a V2 selective agonist and it is used in all the following conditions except?
questions.solutionHtml:
Esophageal varices
  • Desmopressin is V2 receptor selective and not effective in esophageal varices
  • Terlipressin is V1 receptor-selective, so better than desmopressin for esophageal variceal bleeding due to its constructive property.
  • Desmopressin is the drug of choice for central diabetes insipidus and is used in nocturnal enuresis in children, haemophilia and von Willebrand’s Disease



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 643

questions.stem: A 55-year-old male patient was having Dilutional Hyponatremia and increased ADH levels. Which of the following drug will help in the above condition of the patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tolvaptan
  • Patients having Dilutional Hyponatremia and increased ADH levels point towards a diagnosis of SIADH.
  • V2 receptor antagonists like tolvaptan are used in SIADH


  • PHARMACOKINETICS

  • The absolute bioavailability of a dose of tolvaptan is unknown, but at least 40% of the drug is absorbed after oral administration.
  • The onset of effect is two to four hours after a dose is taken, and peak effects occur four to eight hours after administration.
  • After absorption, it is 99% bound to circulating plasma proteins.
  • The volume of distribution is approximately 3 L/kg


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 644

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman comes to the physician for a follow-up examination after presenting with elevated blood pressure readings during her last two visits. After her last visit 2 months ago, she tried controlling her hypertension with weight loss before starting medical therapy, but she has since been unable to lose any weight. Her pulse is 76/min, and her blood pressure is 154/90 mm Hg on the right arm and 155/93 mm Hg on the left arm. She agrees to start treatment with a thiazide diuretic. In response to this treatment, which of the following is most likely to decrease?
questions.solutionHtml:
Urinary calcium excretion
  • Thiazide diuretics (e.g., hydrochlorothiazide) can increase serum calcium levels by decreasing the excretion of calcium in the urine. Other adverse effects include hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, and hyperuricemia.
  • The inhibition of renal Na+-Cl- cotransporters in the early distal tubule causes a net urine loss of positive ions such as sodium. This is compensated by increased renal tubular reabsorption of calcium to maintain electrochemical balance.
  • Thiazide diuretics are used mainly in the treatment of hypertension, but their effect on serum and urinary calcium concentration can also be used for the management of osteoporosis and the prevention of calcium kidney stones.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 628.
